title: 2 Royal Avenue entered community and cultural use
summary: Belfast City Council records 2 Royal Avenue as a community and cultural hub and states that the council has supported the ground floor as a community and cultural space since November 2021.
observed_change: A listed former bank and former retail building entered documented community and cultural use in Belfast city centre.
source_name: Belfast City Council: 2 Royal Avenue venue page and ground-floor expression-of-interest notice
source_date_field: Council page states community and cultural ground-floor use since November 2021; current venue page describes the building as a community and cultural hub.
architect: Belfast City Council, MayWe, and 2 Royal Avenue reuse project team; original Provincial Bank building by William J Barre with later completion by Turner and Williamson.
geometry_source: Curated approximate point from 2 Royal Avenue address stated by Belfast City Council.
geometry_precision: Approximate building point, not a measured ground-floor plan, upper-floor area, kiosk, seating area, or full listed-building boundary.
limitations: The source records council-supported meanwhile cultural use from November 2021 and current venue operation, not a permanent long-term tenancy, full capital-works completion, upper-floor hub opening, visitor numbers, or effects on nearby streets.
duplicate_check_note: Checked existing architecture milestones and local corpus for 2 Royal Avenue, Royal Avenue, 2RA, former Tesco, Tesco Metro, MayWe, event_id, source URL, and source_record_id; no existing manual milestone entry for this cultural-use opening was found.
source_audit_note: Official council venue and notice pages provide the building use, address, history, and month-level use start. Date precision is month because the source gives November 2021 rather than a day-level public opening.

title: W5 LIFE launched at Odyssey Belfast

observed_change: A dedicated STEM learning and skills facility entered documented use within the Odyssey complex.
source_date_field: Odyssey Trust page states W5 LIFE officially launched in November 2022.
architect: The Odyssey Trust, W5, Microsoft, Almac, Belfast Harbour, Nerve Belfast, and W5 LIFE project team; design team not named on the source page.
project_type: learning innovation and STEM skills facility
geometry_source: Curated approximate point from W5 / Odyssey complex address at 2 Queens Quay.
geometry_precision: Approximate complex point, not a measured 20,000 square foot facility footprint, classroom, Dream Space, studio, or full Odyssey parcel.
limitations: The event records launch of W5 LIFE as a distinct facility; it does not restate the wider W5 2021 redevelopment, individual programme launches, participant numbers, partner outcomes, or later OCN registration.
